01 / About

Securing agents.
Building intelligence
we can trust.

I am an Assistant Professor at Northern Arizona University. AI agent security is a central focus of my research: how prompt injection and untrusted tool outputs change an agent's behavior, where attacks enter an agent trajectory, and how to detect and localize failures. My broader work spans natural language processing, fact verification, quantum natural language processing, and access to AI resources.

I lead KALI Lab—Knowledge, Adversaries, Language & Intelligence—where we investigate secure, trustworthy tool-using agents alongside language understanding and emerging computational approaches.

02 / Research

AI agent security
and beyond.

Secure autonomous agents lead a research program spanning language understanding and emerging computational methods.

01

AI agent security

Detecting and localizing prompt-injection attacks in agent trajectories, and understanding when an agent resists or drifts from its intended task.

02

Language & reasoning

Fact verification, knowledge distillation, causal reasoning, and more transferable language systems.

03

Quantum language

Compositional and multilingual foundations for quantum natural language processing.
